But I really, really, don't want to get big, visible muscles, since the idea of having large muscles disgusts me(other people having big muscles doesn't disgust me, I just think the idea of having big muscles personally is very disturbing to me). I suck at running as well, and am out of breath after about 50 seconds.

I did stronglifts about 5 years ago, but stopped after I moved somewhere where there was no gym, and I had kept stalling out at about 90 lbs on the benchpress. I'm hoping to find a way to get stronger and faster without getting big. I've read that if you do very few reps in each set, this can help maximize strength gain and minimize size gains. How practical is this as a long term strategy to gain strength? And are there any other ways to maximize strength and power without getting big muscles?
How to get stronger and faster without getting large muscles?

What do you mean with big? you're not going to get anywhere near the level of a natural body builder if you don't aim for it. I've seen people who do mainly olympic lifts that look like runners.

If you want to get stronger without size keep your reps to 5 or less, resting times between 2-5 minutes, As a beginner (since you lifted 5 years ago) you'll gain some power (how fast you can produce force) too. However after you get over your beginner gains, linear 5 sets x 5 reps won't be enough to make you stronger.

Since it sounds like you're pretty much a tabula rasa, focus on the basics. I'd recommend a regimen like:

  • Couch to 5k
  • Starting Strength or Stronglifts 5x5
  • Calculate caloric needs using IIFYM's calculator and then track everything you eat using MyFitnessPal to ensure you're eating exactly what you need to.

Put together a schedule so you do both of those workouts simultaneously for a combined 5-6 days per week and consistently eat less than your total daily energy expenditure and you're pretty much guaranteed to lose weight while also gaining athletic performance. Once you'd no longer describe yourself as "fat," up your calorie intake (protein in particular) to facilitate more muscle growth & endurance in your training sessions and stay on that track until you start to think you're getting too bulky, and then dial back on the calories again.

IMO you're going to have a tough time being "fast" while you're fat. You'll probably need perform some basic maintenance and fix your body before you'll really start seeing performance gains. Diet is the #1 factor when it comes to body composition. Also, you're not going to just permanently explode into the hulk if you do an intense lifting program. Most fitness models & bodybuilders use steroids because maintaining significant muscle mass naturally is hard. Don't be afraid to lift hard & heavy and tone it back in the unlikely event you think you look too ripped.
Personally I think 5-6 times a week would be too much for someone completely new, and I would focus on the couch to 5k program at first. Just get that stamina up!

I'd say for your situation stronglifts (5x5) would be good, starting strength (3x5) better. For strength without size you want low reps, long rests, explosive movement. If you start getting into the high reps, controlled movements and short rests stuff, you will enter hypertrophy which is where you get most of the muscle mass. For the weight loss start a calorie cut and attempt a 40/30/30 macro. I think that myfitnesspal is a fantastic way to do this, but there are others out there like supertracker. You can strength train while cutting. If you do all this you can basically throttle your muscle size with you diet. Want big muscles? Shift towards 50/30/20 and increase calories. Want to keep it slim? Hold off on cals, keep that 40/30/30. At some point you will plateau if you don't eat more and get bigger, but it sounds like that is what you want.

Would you mind explaining what a "macro" is? I see the term everywhere but nobody ever explains what it means or why it's useful. I doubt a beginner has any clue what a "40/30/30 macro" means. I have been lifting and working out for the past 4 months with great results and have no clue what those terms even mean. I know how many calories I'm supposed to eat in a day, I track them on MFP and that's about as the extent of my "dieting". I don't know what "macros or micros" I'm supposed to be eating...I just know not to eat too many calories and to stick to things like lean protein, lots of veggies and fruits for snacking, non-fat greek yogurt for breakfast etc. It's been working for me, but maybe you can help me understand all this macro/micro stuff.

Sure thing. Macros = Macronutrients = Fat Protein and Carbohydrates. All of your calories come from those three nutrients. Each gram of protein is 4 calories, each gram of carbs is 4 calories and each gram of fat is 9 calories. So if you have two foods and you want to compare them you can look at how many calories each holds, but this doesn't really help so much. You can just eat more of whatever has fewer calories to make them equivalent. So instead its often helpful to look at macronutrient ratios, or macro ratios. This is the ratio of calories from each of the macronutrients in the order carbs/protein/fat. For example cheerios is 73/11/16, and 1% cottage cheese is 28/61/11. By comparing them you can say "if i eat 100 calories of cheerios ill get a lot more carbs for fast energy, but 100 calories of cottage cheese will provide more long lasting protein at the expense of that burst of feel good energy". Getting your macros right allows you to tailor your energy levels with fewer calories, thus aiding in better weight loss.

Micronutrients are basically vitamins. I don't pay attention to them, I just take a multivitamin and hope it gives me what I need. Some people get into micros though and supplement certain vitamins while lifting.

If you're currently out of shape and trying to get strong, you're not going to get "big" the way you think you are. Just start lifting. Start small and work your way up, and don't try to rush your way to heavier lifts. If you want to lose fat, make sure you're doing cardio at least 3 times a week. You're making it sound like accidentally doing a few extra reps will have your muscles bulging out of your arms like some hulking roid rager. That's not how it works. It takes a long time to get big like you're thinking....like years and years of dedicated strength training and proper diet. That doesn't happen in a few weeks or even months.

Also, when trying to break a plateau, it helps immensely when trying to progress if you have a friend go with you to spot. I wouldn't be able to progress nearly as much without someone there spotting me to push through tough sets.
Where do you think strength comes from? In order to get stronger you need to build muscle mass. You aren't going to accidentally Arnold so I think you are being a bit unrealistic here.
